children: New Delhi, Oct. 1 -- The price of 19-kg commercial LPG cylinders was increased across cities from October 1. The prices were hiked just ahead of the festive season, and in the backdrop of the West Asia war that has impacted global energy supplies. In Delhi, the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder rose by Rs.62.50 to Rs.2,810, according to reports.

Commercial LPG prices were increased by Rs.9.50 per 19-kg cylinder in September, following two consecutive monthly reductions of Rs.192 in August and Rs.183.50 in July. Commercial LPG prices had risen by Rs.1,373 per 19-kg cylinder between February and June, from Rs.1,740.50 to Rs.3,113.50, before falling in July and August.
After the hike on October 1, here's what commercial LPG cylinders cost in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and other cities, as per an NDTV report:
Delhi: Price increased by Rs.62.50 to Rs.2,810
Mumbai: Price increased by Rs.63 from Rs.2,701 to Rs.2,764
Chennai: Price increased by Rs.66.50 from Rs.2,916.50 to Rs.2,983
Patna: Prices increased by Rs.71.50 from Rs.3,029 to Rs.3,100.50. This is the highest increase among the cities cited in the report.
Lucknow: Price increased by Rs.62.50 to Rs.2,932.50
Leh: Rs.3,450; Leh continues to be the most expensive state for LPG cylinders.
Tawang: Rs.3,073.50
Ahmedabad: Rs.2,831.50
Kanyakumari: Rs.3,046
Bhopal: Rs.2,815

While the price of commercial LPG cylinders were reportedly increased on October 1, the cost of domestic LPG prices (4.2-kg cylinder) remains same. Here are the current prices as per the Indian Oil website:
Delhi: Rs.942.00
Kolkata: Rs.968.00
Mumbai: Rs.941.50
Chennai: Rs.957.50
Domestic cooking gas rates were increased by Rs.89 per cylinder between March and June after the West Asia crisis led to supply disruptions and a surge in international energy prices

According to ANI, Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices increased by around Rs.16 from Rs.121 per litre to Rs.137 per litre. ATF prices were increased to Rs.137 per litre from Rs.121 for domestic airlines, according to the oil companies.

The latest revision comes after ATF prices were raised by Rs.6.28 per litre, or 5.46 per cent, in September, following a Rs.5 per litre increase in August. ATF accounts for up to 40 per cent of operating costs for airlines, making fuel prices a key cost factor for carriers.

The latest changes are based on movements in international benchmark prices and the rupee-dollar exchange rate. ATF and LPG prices are revised on the first day of every month and can vary across states because of local taxes such as VAT.
Petrol and diesel prices, which were hiked by about Rs.7.50 a litre each in May, too, remained unchanged.
